tips: Famous for their porter. A key stop on the Bermondsey Beer Mile. Open Saturdays.

name: Crate Brewery
description: A canal-side brewery and pizzeria in Hackney Wick with a large outdoor area. Excellent craft beer brewed on site and proper sourdough pizza.
tips: The canal-side setting is lovely. Great pizza and own-brewed beer. Part of the creative Hackney Wick scene.

name: Five Points Brewing Co.
description: A Hackney brewery with a lively taproom serving their range of well-crafted beers. Regular events and food pop-ups in an industrial setting.
tips: Their Pale is one of London's best session beers. The taproom has regular food pop-ups and events.

name: Beavertown Brewery Taproom
description: A large Tottenham taproom from one of London's most popular craft breweries. Tour the brewery, taste the full range, and enjoy food from rotating vendors.
address: Units 17-18, Lockwood Industrial Park, London N17 9QP
tips: Book a brewery tour for the full experience. The Neck Oil IPA is their flagship. Rotating food vendors.

name: London Fields Brewery
description: A Hackney brewery and taproom near London Fields park. Their lager is a London classic. Regular events and a friendly neighbourhood atmosphere.
tips: Their unfiltered lager is excellent. Near London Fields park for a sunny afternoon combo.

name: The Dublin Castle
description: A legendary Camden pub and live music venue that helped launch Madness, Blur, and Amy Winehouse. Sweaty, loud, and absolutely essential for live music fans.
tips: Madness played their first gig here. Still hosting brilliant live music. Check the listings.

name: The Social
description: A Fitzrovia bar and music venue from the Heavenly Recordings label. DJs, live music, and a laid-back creative crowd across two floors.
tips: Run by the Heavenly Recordings label. Great DJs and live music. The basement gets sweaty and brilliant.

name: The Sebright Arms
description: A Bethnal Green pub with a basement music venue hosting live bands and DJs. Regular comedy nights and a friendly East London atmosphere.
tips: The basement venue hosts great grassroots music. Comedy nights are popular. Cheap and cheerful.

name: Oslo
description: A Hackney bar and live music venue in a former railway station ticket office. Excellent programming from live bands to club nights to Sunday jazz.
tips: In a converted railway station ticket office. Varied programming from live music to club nights. Check listings.

name: Rough Trade East
description: An iconic record shop in Brick Lane that doubles as a live music venue. Free in-store gigs from emerging and established artists in a music-lover's paradise.
address: Old Truman Brewery, 91 Brick Ln, London E1 6QL
tips: Free in-store gigs most evenings. Check their website for listings. Browse vinyl while you wait.

name: 229 The Venue
description: A multi-room live music venue and club on Great Portland Street. Regular live gigs and club nights in an intimate West End setting.
tips: A good-sized live venue in the West End. Regular club nights after gigs. Check the lineup.

name: Fold
description: A serious underground club in Canning Town with a Funktion-One sound system and marathon weekend sessions. A pilgrimage site for electronic music devotees.
tips: The sound system is extraordinary. Marathon sessions can run past noon Sunday. For serious electronic music fans.

name: The Cause
description: A non-profit community club and creative space donating profits to charity. Multiple rooms, outdoor areas, and a genuine sense of community purpose.
address: Ashley House, Ashley Rd, London N17 9LZ
tips: All profits go to charity. Multiple rooms and outdoor spaces. A club with a conscience.

name: Venue MOT
description: A raw, underground club in a former MOT garage. Dark, industrial, and focused on quality electronic music with a no-frills approach.
address: Unit 18, Hatcham Park Mews, London SE14 5QA
tips: Raw, industrial, no-frills. The focus is entirely on the music. A proper underground club experience.

name: Colour Factory
description: A warehouse club and event space in Hackney Wick with a large capacity and serious sound system. Hosts major electronic music events and day parties.
tips: Big warehouse space in creative Hackney Wick. Day parties in summer are excellent. Check the lineup.

name: Panda & Sons
description: A hidden cocktail bar behind a vintage barber shop facade. Descend the stairs to find inventive cocktails in a cosy, dimly-lit speakeasy inspired by the Edinburgh original.
tips: Look for the barber shop frontage. The hidden entrance is part of the fun. Creative cocktails with a playful twist.

name: The Grapes Bermondsey
description: A friendly Bermondsey Street pub with craft beers, excellent food, and a welcoming local atmosphere. A great stop on any Bermondsey pub crawl.
tips: On trendy Bermondsey Street with plenty of other bars nearby. Good craft beer selection and pub food.

name: The Beaufort Bar at The Savoy
description: The Savoy's black-and-gold jewel-box cocktail bar — theatrical, midnight-moody, with live jazz on Fridays.
tips: Book for live jazz nights.

name: Artesian at The Langham
description: A legendary cocktail bar in one of London's oldest grand hotels — a former 'World's Best Bar' that keeps the creative bar high.
tips: Dress code: smart. Non-residents welcome.

name: Claridge's Bar
description: Art Deco cocktail bar inside Claridge's — the cocktail list is ultra-classical, the company glamorous, the atmosphere unbeatable.
tips: Books up — come early. The Fumoir is a more intimate alternative.

name: The Fumoir at Claridge's
description: Claridge's tiny Art Deco speakeasy-esque bar — leather armchairs, inlaid lacquerwork, an intimate hideaway.
tips: Only 26 seats. No reservations.

name: 29 Cocktail Bar
description: A miniature Mayfair bar in the Hakkasan group — moodily lit, Asian-inflected cocktails, secretive feel.
tips: Hakkasan Mayfair's cocktail lounge — accepts walk-ins.

name: Swift Borough
description: The Borough branch of the Soho whisky bar — upstairs cocktails, downstairs 200+ whiskies.
tips: Downstairs whisky-only. Cocktail menu upstairs stronger on classics.

name: Satan's Whiskers
description: Bethnal Green cocktail bar with a daily-changing menu written on the wall — a neighbourhood classic with serious drinks.
tips: Walk-in. Hip-hop soundtrack.

name: Lyaness at Sea Containers
description: Ryan Chetiyawardana (Mr Lyan) at Sea Containers London — a showpiece of proprietary 'ingredients'.
tips: Tasting menu £60. Thames views.

name: The Whisky Exchange — Fitz's Lounge
description: Above the Covent Garden whisky shop — tasting sessions, masterclasses, and one of London's largest back-bar whisky selections.
tips: Masterclasses by appointment.

name: Milroy's of Soho
description: London's oldest whisky shop (1964) — the upstairs shop and the basement speakeasy-bar The Vault, 100+ drams.
tips: The Vault basement accessed via a 'secret' bookcase door.

name: Black Rock
description: A whisky-only bar on Christopher Street — flights of expressions, a 150-year-old tree running through the bar.
tips: Tasting flights £25+.

name: Mahiki
description: Mayfair Tiki-basement classic — a favourite of Prince Harry in the noughties, still going with rum buckets and carnival cocktails.
tips: Dress smart-casual. Door policy firm after 10pm.

name: Laki Kane
description: A tropical tiki bar with live hula — three levels, rum classes, a fully immersive Hawaiian experience in Islington.
tips: Rum-masterclass is a lovely evening.

name: Little Mercies
description: Crouch End's new-wave cocktail bar — ingredient-led drinks, vegan-focused menu, dark and intimate.
tips: Book ahead — tiny room.

name: Tonkotsu Selfie
description: Pioneering London rum bar — rare rum expressions, daiquiri-centric menu, in a tiny Fitzrovia space.
tips: Small and popular — book ahead.

name: Soma
description: A Fitzrovia cocktail bar with a no-technology policy — phones encouraged to be silenced, menu built around Indian ingredients.
tips: Walk-in friendly pre-8pm.

name: The Prospect of Whitby
description: London's oldest riverside pub (1520) in Wapping — flagstone floors, a hanging gallows in the courtyard, Dickensian charm.
tips: The hangman's noose in the beer garden is grim fun.

name: The Town of Ramsgate
description: A 500-year-old Wapping pub with a tidal Thames stair — Captain Bligh drank here the night before Mutiny on the Bounty.
tips: Walk the Wapping Old Stairs at low tide.

name: The Dove Hammersmith
description: A 17th-century Thames-side pub with the smallest bar in the UK and a rose-covered riverside terrace.
tips: Watch the Oxford-Cambridge boat race from here.

name: The Old Ship W6
description: A 16th-century Thames pub in Hammersmith — with river terraces and a real-feel village atmosphere.
tips: One of the best Thames Path stops.

name: The White Cross
description: Richmond's riverside pub — famously floods at high tide; locals watch the drinkers wade out.
tips: Watch tide tables — flood at high tide is a photo-op.

name: The Jerusalem Tavern
description: A Clerkenwell gem (1720) — St Peter's Brewery's tiny tap, feels like a time capsule.
tips: Tiny — squeeze onto a bench or stand in the alley.

name: The Harp
description: Covent Garden's real-ale classic — a narrow room of 20+ cask ales and craft beers, a two-time CAMRA National Pub of the Year.
tips: Pork pies and Scotch eggs on the bar.

name: The Princess Louise
description: An astonishing 1872 Victorian gin palace in Holborn — etched mirrors, ornate tilework, and a horseshoe bar.
tips: Cheapest pub in central London — Sam Smith's prices. Gorgeous.

name: The Cittie of Yorke
description: A huge 15th-century-style pub on Chancery Lane — cathedral-like main hall, wine vats behind the bar, Samuel Smith's ales.
tips: Dark snugs along the wall are beloved by barristers.

name: The Lamb Bloomsbury
description: A Bloomsbury stained-glass Victorian — etched glass snob-screens on the bar, Dickens mentioned it in 'Barnaby Rudge'.
tips: One of the few remaining pubs with snob-screens intact.

name: The Red Lion St James's
description: A magnificent 1871 Victorian gin palace in Mayfair — bevelled mirrors, ornate plasterwork, ornate lamps.
address: 2 Duke of York St, London SW1Y 6JP
tips: Stained-glass windows worth a close look.

name: The Salisbury
description: A gorgeous Victorian Theatre-District pub with brass oil lamps, cut-glass mirrors, and rich red velvet.
tips: A 10-minute wait for a seat in peak hours.

name: The Guinea Grill
description: Mayfair's Georgian chop-house pub — a 1423 licensing date, a pie-shop at the back, Mayfair-elite clientele.
tips: Beef-and-kidney pie at the back counter is a London classic.

name: The Star Tavern
description: Belgravia pub, hidden in a mews — the Great Train Robbers reputedly planned their 1963 heist in a private room upstairs.
tips: Book a table for Sunday roast.

name: The Coach & Horses Soho
description: Jeffrey Bernard's legendary Soho pub — a literary boozer now transformed (gentrified) but still a Soho landmark.
tips: Drinks on Saturdays feature the 'Private Eye' lunch.

name: The Golden Lion St James's
description: Opposite Christie's in St James's — an 1899 Victorian with a preserved upstairs and gold-leaf bar.
tips: Upstairs is quieter — ask if open.

name: The Dog House
description: A Kennington craft-beer pub — 20+ taps, friendly neighbourhood feel, a good refuge after the Imperial War Museum.
tips: Strong changing cask selection.

name: BrewDog Waterloo
description: A cavernous craft-beer cathedral in a vault under Waterloo Station — BrewDog's largest UK bar, 60+ taps.
tips: Combine with Leake Street graffiti tunnel outside.

name: Five Points Brewing Co Taproom
description: Hackney brewery's taproom and shop — 15+ taps, industrial setting, frequent brewery tours.
tips: Second taproom at Big Penny Social in Walthamstow.

name: The Kernel Brewery Taproom
description: Bermondsey's legendary brewery taproom — open Saturday only, part of the 'Bermondsey Beer Mile'.
address: Arch 11, Dockley Rd Industrial Estate, London SE16 3SF
tips: Open Saturdays only 9-4pm. The Beer Mile is a full-day affair.

name: Fourpure Brewing
description: Bermondsey Beer Mile stop — modern-industrial taproom with 20+ taps.
address: 22 Bermondsey Trading Estate, Rotherhithe New Rd, London SE16 3LL
tips: Weekends only for the taproom.

name: Anspach & Hobday
description: A Bermondsey Beer Mile brewery and taproom — 16+ rotating taps, outdoor space, very community-feel.
tips: Open Thu-Sun with live events most weekends.

name: Moor Beer Vaults
description: Bermondsey taproom of this Bristol-born brewery — natural, unfiltered ales in an industrial rail arch.
tips: Open Wed-Sun.

name: Cloudwater Taproom
description: Manchester-born craft brewery's Bermondsey outpost — rotating rare releases, a serious IPA specialist.
address: Unit 2, 24-28 Rich Industrial Estate, London SE15 1BS
tips: Open Thu-Sun only. Check current location.

name: Fox at Saint John's Hotel
description: Haymarket hotel rooftop bar with outdoor terrace views toward Piccadilly — fairly-priced cocktails, quiet atmosphere.
tips: Book ahead for rooftop.

name: Radio Rooftop at ME London
description: 10th-floor Covent Garden rooftop bar — wraparound Thames-to-West-End views, DJ weekends.
tips: Book a window table for sunset.

name: Bar Elba
description: Waterloo's summer-only rooftop bar — Art Deco-themed, DJ nights, a sleek view over the South Bank.
address: The Sidings, 5 Leake St, London SE1 7NN
tips: Indoor in winter. Book Fri/Sat.

name: Queen of Hoxton Rooftop
description: A changing-themed rooftop bar — tipi in winter, garden in summer, always with big-screen sports, DJ nights, and street food.
tips: Free before 7pm most nights.

name: Netil 360
description: Hackney rooftop bar above Netil Market — panoramic East-London skyline, sunset DJs, casual atmosphere.
tips: Fridays and weekends only. Entry from Netil Market.

name: Dalston Roof Park
description: Summer-only rooftop with cinema screenings, DJs, and street food — multicoloured seating, East London sunset views.
address: Bootstrap Building, Ashwin St, London E8 3DL
tips: Book for rooftop cinema. Summer only.

name: The Culpeper Rooftop Garden
description: An 1850s Spitalfields pub with a rooftop herb-garden bar — kitchen growing its own vegetables, seasonal cocktails.
tips: Summer only. Tiny — arrive early.

name: London Cocktail Club
description: Six-branch chain of laid-back cocktail bars — proper drinks, loud music, bargain-bin pricing (£6 happy hour).
tips: Happy hour £6 cocktails 5-7pm.

name: Be At One
description: UK-wide cocktail bar chain with multiple London branches — buzzing, affordable, 2-for-1 happy hours.
tips: Happy hour 5-7pm daily.

name: Simmons Bar King's Cross
description: Quirky-themed cocktail bar — kitsch decor, big table service, cocktails in teapots. A lively-hen-party favourite.
tips: Good pre-club spot.

name: Cahoots
description: A 1940s WWII-themed basement-in-a-Tube-carriage bar — dress-up encouraged, vintage cocktails and air raid sirens.
tips: Smart-casual dress-up strongly encouraged. Book well ahead.

name: Mr Fogg's Gin Parlour
description: Covent Garden Mr Fogg's branch with 200+ gins — the theme is Phileas Fogg's aunt's drawing room.
tips: Gin flights £24. Victorian dress-up nights.

name: Mr Fogg's House of Botanicals
description: Victoria-themed bar in Fitzrovia — tropical flora, cocktails based on plants, live entertainment.
tips: Afternoon tea with cocktails a speciality.

name: The Bletchley
description: A WW2-Bletchley-Park-themed cocktail bar — you're given a codebreaker assignment, and your cocktails arrive in coded glasses.
tips: Book the 'Junior Cipher Clerk' or 'Senior Cipher Clerk' experience.

name: Hawksmoor Guildhall Bar
description: City chop-house bar of Hawksmoor Guildhall — classic cocktails, a good whisky list, and pre-dinner ease.
tips: Bar accepts walk-ins. Dining room bookable.

name: Chiltern Firehouse Bar
description: The members' and guests' bar at Chiltern Firehouse — exclusive, celeb-heavy, beautifully crafted drinks.
tips: Non-guests must book via the restaurant.

name: The East Bar at Sketch
description: Sketch's David Shrigley-designed toilet pods and east-bar alter ego — Instagram-mad, genuinely creative.
tips: Photogenic toilets — yes, really.

name: BYOC
description: 'Bring Your Own Cocktail' — a Kingsbridge 'prohibition-era' members' bar where you bring spirits and they mix.
tips: Ticket price (£40pp) covers the service; bring your own bottle.

name: The Distillery Portobello Road
description: Hotel-with-a-gin-distillery on Portobello Road — gin bar, gin library, and gin masterclasses on the same four-storey site.
tips: Gin masterclass £125 includes gin-making.

name: The Ginstitute
description: Portobello Road gin school — spend 3 hours distilling your own gin to take home. Part of The Distillery.
tips: 3-hour masterclass. Leave with a 70cl bottle of your gin.

name: Beefeater Gin Distillery Tour
description: The Kennington distillery where Beefeater has been made since 1958 — working still, museum, tasting bar.
tips: Tour includes tastings — book ahead.

name: Sipsmith Distillery Tour
description: Chiswick-based Sipsmith — London's first new gin distillery in 200 years when it opened in 2009. Working copper stills on show.
tips: Tour includes 5 g&t tastings. Weekends book ahead.

name: Bimber Distillery
description: Acton single-malt whisky distillery — London's only whisky distillery. Tours include serious tastings.
tips: Tour + tasting £40. Whisky-lovers' pilgrimage.

name: East London Liquor Company
description: Bow Wharf's gin, vodka, and whisky distillery — working stills, bar, and restaurant in one place.
tips: Tours and tastings bookable. Restaurant open Wed-Sun.

name: Printworks Legacy (reopening Drumsheds)
description: The former printing plant that became one of London's biggest clubs — now reincarnated at Drumsheds in Tottenham.
tips: Meridian Water station. Check Drumsheds website for events.

name: FOLD
description: East London underground techno club — cavernous Canning Town warehouse, serious sound system.
tips: Community-feel, member-led. ID and booking ahead.

name: The Cause
description: East London's community-driven club with a rotating DJ roster — formerly a garage complex, now a multi-floor venue.
tips: Pay-what-you-can nights support local charities.

name: Lighthouse
description: Battersea's roof-terrace club-bar — summer garden, sunset views, DJ nights into the early hours.
tips: Booking essential. Summer terrace.

name: Oval Space
description: A Bethnal Green warehouse turned club — floor-to-ceiling windows framing the gasholders, eclectic booking policy.
address: The Oval, 29-32 The Oval, London E2 9DT
tips: Events run most weekends.

name: Annabel's
description: The world-famous Mayfair private members' club — old-school glamour, opulent interiors, non-members can attend selected events.
tips: Members or member's guests only.

name: Moda
description: A Mayfair club nestled in the Hotel Café Royal — a chic alternative to the Mayfair big-hitters.
tips: Dress code enforced.

name: Heaven
description: London's iconic gay nightclub since 1979 — under Charing Cross station arches, three dancefloors, hosting G-A-Y nights.
tips: Saturdays are G-A-Y nights — biggest crowd.

name: The Two Brewers Clapham
description: Clapham's legendary gay cabaret pub since 1980 — live drag shows, a lively club upstairs.
tips: Drag bingo Thursdays. Cabaret most nights.

name: Royal Vauxhall Tavern
description: South London's oldest gay pub (1863) — Grade II-listed, a Lily Savage (Paul O'Grady) landmark.
tips: Sunday cabaret. Drag nights Thursday-Saturday.

name: Eagle London
description: Vauxhall gay pub and club — a much-loved leather/bear scene, weekend DJ nights, Sunday afternoon drinks.
tips: Sundays 'Horse Meat Disco' is legendary.

name: LAB Bar
description: Soho's original cocktail training ground (1996) — drinks menu is an index of modern cocktail history.
tips: Late-night crowd. Upstairs quieter.

name: Sidecar
description: Haggerston cocktail bar from the Happiness Forgets team — classic drinks, small-plates food.
tips: Walk-in-friendly. Bar seats and a few tables.

name: Bar Pepito
description: A tiny sherry and cured-meat bar in King's Cross, run by the Camino group — 20 sherries by the glass, tapas.
tips: Sherry flights. The iberico-ham flatbread is a snack classic.

name: Gordon's Wine Bar
description: London's oldest wine bar (1890) — candle-lit vaults in a basement under Villiers Street, 100+ wines by the glass, cheese boards.
tips: Arrive before 5pm for a candle-lit seat. No reservations.

name: Vinoteca
description: A modern wine bar and restaurant in multiple locations — huge wine list priced at retail +£10 corkage.
tips: Buy a wine retail and drink it in for £10 corkage.

name: Terroirs
description: Charing Cross's natural-wine pioneer (2008) — a warm, lived-in wine bar with a French-leaning bistro menu.
tips: Pre-theatre menu excellent.

name: The Remedy
description: A tiny Fitzrovia wine bar and kitchen — chalked-up specials, natural-leaning list, short menu.
tips: Tiny — arrive at opening 5pm.

name: Peckham's Wine Bar (Brixton Wine Bar)
description: Peckham's hyper-local wine bar — natural, organic, biodynamic wines with sourdough-forward small plates.
tips: Book ahead. Tiny room, serious wine.

name: Shrub & Shutter
description: Brixton cocktail bar with house-made shrubs, sodas, and syrups — ingredient-led cocktails, neighbourhood feel.
tips: Ingredient-led menu changes often.

name: Hootananny
description: Brixton reggae-and-live-music bar — free entry most nights, ska and dub DJs Friday and Saturday.
tips: Monday evening open-mic night.

name: Brixton Jamm
description: Brixton's long-standing music venue — all-nighter clubs, live gigs, soundsystems on Akerman Road.
tips: Check listings — very eclectic programming.

name: Passing Clouds (closed) — Pickle Factory
description: The Pickle Factory — Hackney's tiny-intimate dance club with house and disco nights, perfect sound system.
tips: Friday and Saturday only. 150-cap.

name: Lounge Bohemia
description: A Shoreditch secret-buzzer-only cocktail bar — no dress code but book far ahead, slow-drink philosophy, strict no-suits policy.
tips: Reservations only. No one over 35 allowed apparently.

name: Black Book Bar
description: A Soho literary cocktail bar — menu inspired by famous novels, with drinks like The Great Gatsby and The Shining.
tips: Request-the-bartender cocktails ('make me something based on my favourite author').

name: 12:51 by James Cochran
description: Islington cocktail bar and kitchen — chef-led drinks, impeccable Afro-Caribbean-influenced small plates.
tips: Tasting menu is the move.

name: The Blue Posts Kingly Court
description: A 16th-century coaching inn rebuilt as a three-floor pub-and-restaurant complex in Kingly Court — rooftop, basement, and Palomar team food.
tips: Rooftop cocktail bar on top; pub in the middle; restaurant in the basement.

name: Griffin
description: The Shoreditch pub that's been there before, during, and after gentrification — working-class East End cornerstone.
tips: Pool table and no frills. Pre-club pint classic.

name: The Queen's Head Piccadilly
description: A sliver of a pub on Denman Street — one of Soho's oldest Tudor-beamed survivors, now a lovely neighbourhood local.
tips: Strong selection of ales — often with a cask guest.

name: Mother Kelly's
description: Bethnal Green railway-arch craft-beer bar — 23 taps, American-leaning selection, Italian-American food menu.
tips: Family-friendly during day, lively late.

name: The Princess of Wales
description: A Highbury Georgian pub — beautifully preserved, a beer garden, strong Sunday-lunch-forward following.
tips: Book for Sunday roast.

name: The Earl of Essex
description: Islington's craft-beer pub — 18 rotating taps, sharp beer knowledge, and a stained-glass Victorian interior.
tips: Excellent cider list too.

name: The Pineapple Kentish Town
description: A quirky Kentish Town community pub — saved from closure in 2002 by its regulars, now a local institution.
tips: Grade II-listed. Thai food at the back.

name: Hole in the Wall
description: Waterloo railway-arch pub — loud, cheap, a grime-free survivor of old-Waterloo charm. Arch 5 under the platforms.
tips: Trains thunder overhead.

name: Beer Merchants Tap
description: Hackney Wick taproom of the UK's biggest craft-beer importer — 24 rotating taps, Belgian-heavy, plus a bottle shop.
tips: Knowledgeable staff. Excellent Belgian selection.

name: The Scarsdale Tavern
description: A pretty corner pub on Edwardes Square, Kensington — wisteria-covered in summer, log fire in winter.
tips: The pub's corner of Edwardes Square is one of London's most photogenic.

name: The Cross Keys Chelsea
description: Chelsea's oldest pub (1712) — Whistler, Turner and Dylan Thomas drank here; now a sharp gastropub.
tips: Sunday roast is a Chelsea institution.

name: The Antelope
description: A 1780s Belgravia tucked-away pub — unreformed, small, with a flawless pint and deep sporting culture.
tips: Match days busy with rugby fans.

name: The Cow
description: Tom Conran's Notting Hill gastropub — Guinness, oysters, and Dublin-style character since 1998.
tips: Oysters and a pint of Guinness is the order. Dining room upstairs.

name: The Audley
description: Artist Damien Hirst-owned Mayfair pub — 19th-century-grand, restored with his art dotted throughout.
tips: First-floor Mount Street restaurant needs booking.

name: The Horse & Groom
description: A gorgeously preserved Belgravia mews pub — flower boxes, a tiny back bar, a village feel.
tips: Mews-tucked — easily missed. Look for the flowerboxes.

name: The Windmill Mayfair
description: A 1729 Mayfair pub famous for its pies — chef-owned by Michael O'Hare, generous pies since 1729.
tips: Book upstairs for a table if eating.

name: The Harp Tottenham
description: Craft beer and cider in a Tottenham Court Road Victorian pub — narrow room, 8 rotating cask ales.
tips: Ploughman's board a nice snack.

name: The Bricklayer's Arms
description: An old-school Putney pub — a haunt of rowers during Boat Race week, ale-first, free juke-box.
tips: Riverside, short walk from Putney Bridge.

name: The Southampton Arms
description: Kentish Town community ale-and-cider pub — 18 taps, coal fire, a dog-friendly atmosphere.
tips: Pork pies the staple snack.

name: The King's Arms Waterloo
description: Cosy Waterloo pub on Roupell Street — unchanged since 1890, terraced Georgian street setting.
tips: Thai food at the back. Street is a Dickensian film-location favourite.

name: The Euston Tap
description: Twin gatehouses either side of Euston Road turned craft-beer pubs — 40+ taps between the two West and East lodges.
tips: Inside spiral staircase to the upstairs tasting room.

name: The Parcel Yard
description: King's Cross Station's grand Victorian pub above the platforms — Fuller's pies and ales, a quieter commuter retreat.
tips: Full restaurant inside — great for pre-train food.

name: The Betjeman Arms
description: St Pancras Station's elegant first-floor pub — named for the poet who saved St Pancras, statue of him watches over diners.
address: Unit 53, St Pancras Station, London N1C 4QL
tips: Gets busy pre-Eurostar.

name: Simmons Euston
description: Quirky-themed cocktail bar in Euston — teapot cocktails, bright decor, a strong hen-party crowd.
tips: Group deals good value.

name: La Bodega Negra
description: Mexican restaurant and basement bar in Soho — taqueria upstairs, late-night cocktail bar downstairs accessed via a 'sex shop' front.
tips: The 'Adult Shop' front is a tongue-in-cheek disguise — don't be deterred.

name: La Bodega Negra Café
description: The brighter upstairs of La Bodega Negra — Mexican small-plates and margaritas, street-level on Moor Street.
tips: Walk-in-friendly café upstairs.

name: Ceviche
description: Martin Morales's lively Pisco-and-ceviche bar in Soho — Peruvian street food and Pisco sours.
tips: Pisco flights. Happy hour 5-7pm.

name: Casita Andina
description: Soho Andean restaurant-bar — tapas-style Peruvian small plates and cocktails, a sister to Andina.
tips: Downstairs Pisco bar opens late.

name: Peyote
description: Cooper & Eve's Notting Hill Mexican spot — the hacienda-chic elder sister to the Peyotito spin-off.
tips: Tequila tasting flights available.

name: Ojo Rojo
description: A Fitzrovia Mexican mezcaleria — tacos, mezcal flights, sharp-drinks bar.
tips: Mezcal tasting flights.

name: Cantina Laredo
description: Seven Dials Mexican — tableside-made guacamole, enchiladas, and the best margaritas in Covent Garden.
address: 10 Upper St Martin's Ln, London WC2H 9FB
tips: Bottomless brunch weekends.

name: Ermal's Cocktail Club
description: Fitzrovia cocktail pop-up — former Experimental Cocktail Club bartender, natural-wine forward cocktails.
tips: Check Instagram for current location and events.

name: Barts
description: Chelsea speakeasy behind an 'apartment block' door — 1920s theme, ring a bell, and the door opens.
tips: Dress up strongly encouraged.

name: The Blind Pig
description: Social Eating House's upstairs speakeasy — 1930s-themed low-lit Soho cocktail bar, classic-cocktail-forward.
tips: Booking recommended — smaller room.

name: KOL Mezcaleria
description: The basement mezcaleria of Michelin-starred KOL — 100+ agave spirits, Mexican street snacks.
tips: Walk-in-friendly downstairs. Dining room above is Michelin-starred.

name: Savage Garden at Double Tree Tower Hill
description: 12th-floor rooftop bar — views of Tower Bridge, the Shard, and the City. Indoor and outdoor terraces.
tips: Book ahead for terrace.

name: Madison
description: Roof-terrace restaurant-bar beside St Paul's Cathedral — the cathedral is the view, gin-and-tonic trolley the drink.
tips: The best close-up view of St Paul's dome in London.

name: Rumpus Room
description: Mondrian Hotel's riverside rooftop — a cocktail bar with Thames-to-Tate Modern views.
tips: Book for sunset on Friday/Saturday.

name: Aqua Spirit
description: Aqua Shard at the top of Regent Street — a glamorous bar atop the Regent Street Hong Kong building.
tips: Aqua Nueva for seating; Aqua Kyoto upstairs.

name: Jin Bo Law
description: Dorsett City Hotel's 14th-floor rooftop cocktail bar — Asian-inspired menu, sweeping City views.
tips: Indoor-outdoor terrace.

name: The French Pub
description: A tiny Fitzrovia wine bar — French-only list, no bottles over £40, an insider's secret.
tips: No cocktails. Just wine.

name: Remedy Wine Bar
description: Fitzrovia natural-wine bar — chalked-up daily specials, a six-counter-seat room.
tips: Book — just 12 seats.

name: Peckham Cellars
description: Peckham wine bar and shop — Tomasz Wasiuk's biodynamic wine list, small plates, walk-in-friendly.
tips: Retail shop at the front.

name: P. Franco
description: A Clapton wine shop-bar — buy a bottle at retail and drink it in, with a rotating guest chef.
tips: Walk-in. 25 seats max.

name: Top Cuvée
description: Highbury wine shop-bar — retail+£10 corkage, natural-wine list, lo-fi café vibe.
tips: Book in advance — small space.

name: Levant
description: A Marylebone basement Middle Eastern restaurant and cocktail bar — belly dancers nightly, hubbly-bubbly pipes.
tips: Belly dancing from 8pm Fri-Sat.

name: Kazbar Clapham
description: North-African-themed late-night bar — mezze, belly dancing, shisha terrace.
tips: Open late — 3am weekends.

name: Elephant Westbourne Park
description: Westbourne Park pub with a leafy garden — cask ale, weekly quiz, neighbourhood feel.
tips: Tuesdays pub quiz popular.

name: The Harwood Arms Bar
description: Ground-floor bar of the Michelin-starred Harwood Arms pub — walk-in for cask ales while you wait.
tips: No reservations in the bar.

name: The Jugged Hare
description: A City gastropub specialising in game — taxidermy on the walls, game-forward menu, a favourite of Barbican-goers.
tips: Seasonal game menu.

name: The Clerk & Well
description: A Clerkenwell Green boutique-gastropub — craft beers, Sunday roast, a lovely little beer garden.
tips: Garden in summer — a rare Clerkenwell find.

name: The Hand in Hand Wimbledon
description: A charming Wimbledon Common pub — low-ceilinged, dog-friendly, a local-first feel.
tips: Combine with a Wimbledon Common walk.

name: The Fox & Hounds Chelsea
description: A local-feeling Chelsea pub on Passmore Street — beer garden, big-screen sports, a neighbourhood refuge.
tips: Football and rugby on weekends.

name: The Crobar
description: A legendary Soho rock-and-metal dive bar — metal on the jukebox, late nights, strong pours.
tips: Cash-only. Open very late.

name: The Toucan
description: Soho's tiny Irish pub — Guinness, Jameson, and an unreformed dive-bar vibe near Tottenham Court Road.
tips: Standing-room-only at peak times.

name: Ye Olde Mitre
description: A 1546 Ely-Place pub hidden down an alley — Queen Elizabeth I reputedly danced around its cherry tree.
tips: Access via narrow Ely Place alley. Closed weekends.

name: The Blackfriar
description: An Art Nouveau confection (1905) — mosaic friezes, bronze sculptures of friars, marble interiors. Opposite Blackfriars station.
tips: Stand at the bar just to study the mosaics.

name: The Viaduct Tavern
description: A 1869 Victorian gin palace opposite the Old Bailey — gilded mirrors, etched glass, and old Newgate Prison cells in the basement.
tips: Ask to see the Newgate Prison cells downstairs.

name: The Counting House
description: A former City banking hall turned Fuller's pub — high ceilings, marble columns, chandeliers, and pies.
tips: Quiet on weekends — City-weekday buzz.

name: Hamilton Hall
description: A grand Wetherspoon's housed in the old Great Eastern Hotel ballroom — ornate plasterwork, gilded chandeliers.
tips: Remarkable interior at Wetherspoon's prices.

name: Crown & Sceptre
description: A decent Walthamstow pub with a beer garden — a genuine neighbourhood local.
tips: Walthamstow Central close.

name: The Carpenter's Arms
description: A Cheshire Street corner pub — famously bought by the Kray twins for their mother in 1966; now a normal, lovely pub.
tips: Walls lined with Kray-related memorabilia.

name: The Cross Kings
description: A King's Cross traditional pub — unreformed, pool table, late-night crowd after parties.
tips: Open late on weekends.

name: The Betsey Trotwood
description: A Farringdon Victorian pub and live-music venue — basement gigs with a singer-songwriter focus.
tips: Gigs most nights — £5-10.

name: The Castle
description: Clerkenwell Victorian pub — the only pub in Britain licensed as a pawnbrokers (you can, in theory, pawn your drink deposit)
tips: Three golden balls on the sign — the pawnbroker symbol.

name: The Three Compasses
description: A Hornsey Victorian pub — decent beer garden, live music, a North-London institution.
tips: Friday blues nights popular.

name: Nightjar Carnaby
description: A more accessible Carnaby outpost of Shoreditch's Nightjar — live jazz most nights, lavish 1920s-style cocktails.
tips: Live music 8pm onwards.

name: Pizza Express Jazz Club Soho
description: A surprising jazz venue in the basement of a pizzeria — major US jazz artists play here regularly.
tips: Dinner + gig recommended — the pizza is the byproduct.

name: Roundhouse
description: Camden's Grade II-listed circular engine shed turned arts venue — big-hitting gigs, comedy, and circus.
tips: Studio theatre hosts smaller shows.

name: The Lexington Live
description: Angel's live-music upstairs room — 200 capacity, alt/indie/punk lineups, a London-band-incubator.
tips: Gigs most nights. Free after-party.

name: The Garage
description: Highbury & Islington's 600-cap indie/punk/rock venue — sweaty, sticky, a rite of passage.
tips: The smaller Garage Upstairs hosts new acts.

name: Electric Ballroom
description: Camden's 1,100-cap live-music venue — a punk-era classic, still programmes rock, metal, and indie.
tips: Saturday market also runs on-site.

name: The Dublin Castle
description: Camden's tiny Madness-breakthrough pub — 180-cap back room, indie gigs most nights, a London music-history spot.
tips: Cash-only. Gigs nightly.

name: Windmill Brixton
description: Tiny Brixton pub-and-venue — launching pad for Fat White Family, shame, Black Country New Road, a cult room for new guitar bands.
tips: 80-cap. Gigs nightly. Cash-only.

name: The Shacklewell Arms
description: Dalston's cult live-music pub — indie, punk, queer club nights. 250-cap back room.
tips: Gigs most nights — check Resident Advisor.

name: MOTH Club
description: Hackney Central club in a former British Legion hall — gold-glitter ceiling, cheap drinks, cult live gigs and DJ nights.
address: Old Trades Hall, Valette St, London E9 6NU
tips: The gold-glitter ceiling is an Instagram favourite.

name: Rich Mix
description: Shoreditch's community-led cinema-and-music venue — three cinema screens, a live-music studio, and a bar.
tips: Weekly world-music nights and South Asian cinema.

name: Café OTO Dalston
description: The UK's leading experimental-music venue — gigs most nights, a daytime café, a brilliantly curated programme.
tips: Café by day; gigs from 7:30pm.

name: Wigmore Hall
description: A recital hall on Wigmore Street — one of the best chamber music venues in the world, with renowned acoustics and a 552-seat ceiling fresco.
tips: Sunday morning coffee concerts £20 are the bargain.

name: Kings Place
description: A purpose-built classical-and-jazz music venue at King's Cross — two halls, brilliant acoustics, rigorous programming.
tips: Hall One for chamber; Hall Two for jazz.

name: Cadogan Hall
description: Former Christian Science church turned chamber-and-jazz hall — 900-seat, the English Chamber Orchestra's home.
tips: Saturday morning jazz breakfasts £15 with pastries included.

name: Clapham Grand
description: A Victorian theatre turned music venue — 1,500-cap, classic indie and pop shows, a grand stepped auditorium.
tips: Cabaret and bingo nights between gigs.

name: O2 Shepherd's Bush Empire
description: A 2,000-cap historic Shepherd's Bush music venue — original 1903 Frank Matcham music hall.
tips: Balcony seats the quietest view.

name: Alexandra Palace Theatre
description: An 1875 Victorian theatre restored within Ally Pally — intimate wooden auditorium, 1,300-cap, gigs and events.
tips: Separate from the big Ally Pally arena — smaller, more atmospheric.

name: Paradise by Way of Kensal Green
description: Kensal Green's gothic-glam pub-and-gig-venue — antiques, taxidermy, and a lively stage in the back room.
tips: Sunday roast extraordinary.

name: The Drayton Arms
description: Kensington theatre-pub — 70-seat fringe theatre upstairs, gastropub downstairs.
tips: Check theatre listings for fringe shows.

name: Lauderdale House Café
description: Highgate's 16th-century house with a garden-café — Lauderdale also hosts evening jazz and cabaret.
tips: Check programme for Friday evening cabaret.

name: The Boogaloo
description: A Highgate rock-and-roll pub with a free-for-all jukebox — Shane MacGowan's favourite, cult live music nights.
tips: Pogues song of the week plays on Fridays.

name: The Lock Tavern
description: Camden's music-industry-favourite pub — two DJs every weekend, a terrace with canal view.
tips: Roof terrace in summer essential.

name: The Good Mixer
description: Camden's Britpop shrine — Blur, Oasis, Pulp all drank here in the 1990s, now a friendly community local.
tips: Pub-rock jukebox. Unreformed.

name: The Albany
description: A Deptford Grade II-listed theatre, music, and community venue — a 500-cap auditorium with diverse programming.
tips: Free weekly community nights.

name: The Social
description: Heavenly Recordings' pub-and-club off Oxford Street — cult indie gigs, spoken word, and a strong jukebox.
tips: Heavenly Social DJ nights are legendary.

name: The Booking Office 1869
description: The St Pancras Renaissance Hotel's grand bar — 29-metre-long bar under a Gothic vaulted ceiling.
tips: The only way to experience the St Pancras interior without being a guest.

name: Aqua Kyoto
description: Regent Street rooftop Japanese — sushi, robata, and a cocktail bar with St James's views.
tips: Bar accepts walk-ins; restaurant bookable.

name: Aqua Nueva
description: Regent Street Spanish rooftop — tapas, sangria, skyline terrace.
tips: Siblings Aqua Spirit (cocktails) and Aqua Kyoto (Japanese) share the rooftop.

name: Paradise Soho
description: Sri Lankan bar-and-restaurant on Rupert Street — arrack cocktails, serious Sri Lankan curries, a buzzing crowd.
tips: Arrack flights available.

name: Los Mochis
description: Notting Hill Mexican-Japanese fusion — sushi, tacos, mezcal cocktails, club DJs late nights.
tips: Broadgate sister has rooftop skyline views.

name: The Phoenix Club
description: Cavendish Square private members' club with late licence — 3am on weekends.
tips: Members or member's guests only. Annual membership required.

name: Pedlers
description: Peckham bar-restaurant-club — Rye Lane late-night hang with DJs, natural wine, street food.
tips: Open late weekends; DJ from 10pm Fridays.

name: Aubaine
description: French brasserie chain — locations across Mayfair, Selfridges, and Marylebone. Reliable pit-stop while shopping.
tips: Terrace seats in warmer months.

name: Bar Americano
description: Tiny stand-up-only cocktail bar in Mayfair — six seats, a classic Italian aperitivo menu.
tips: Walk-in: if a seat's free, it's yours.

name: Wine at 74
description: A Borough Market wine bar run by Corney & Barrow — 100+ wines by glass in a lovely Victorian dining room.
tips: Wine-pairing tastings on selected evenings.

name: Pitt Cue Co
description: American-smokehouse restaurant-bar in a City arch — bourbon, cocktails, rib-heavy menu.
address: 1 The Avenue, Devonshire Sq, London EC2M 4YP
tips: Bourbon flight a highlight.

name: Nine Lives Bar
description: Tropicana-themed cocktail bar in London Bridge — house rum distillery upstairs, tiki cocktails downstairs.
tips: Distillery tours on Saturdays.

name: Lamb Tavern Leadenhall
description: A Leadenhall Market Victorian pub (1780) — old mahogany, etched glass, and a City crowd after work.
tips: Closed weekends.

name: Nag's Head Covent Garden
description: McMullen's tiny pub tucked behind Covent Garden — unreformed, tile-bar, a theatre district gem.
tips: Fish and chips their specialty.

name: The Luggage Room
description: A Marylebone Georgian-themed speakeasy — discreet entrance, 1920s cocktails, live jazz on weekends.
tips: Inside London Marriott Grosvenor Square.

name: Nutbourne
description: A Battersea wine bar-restaurant — English wines from the family's own Nutbourne vineyard, modern British cooking.
tips: English wine flight £18.

name: Pantechnicon
description: Belgravia Japanese-Scandinavian fusion — a sunlit rooftop bar, top-floor cocktail terrace, and Eldr restaurant on ground floor.
tips: Rooftop indoor-outdoor terrace books up.

name: Rotunda Bar King's Cross
description: The Rotunda bar at Kings Place — riverside terrace overlooking Battlebridge Basin, ideal before a Kings Place concert.
tips: Sunset terrace in summer.

name: The Spread Eagle Camden
description: A large Camden pub with a Victorian exterior — live rock music at the back room, ordinary pub up front.
tips: Check listings for comedy nights.

name: The Crown Greenwich
description: A traditional pub a block from Greenwich Market — cask ales and Fuller's London Pride, a proper neighbourhood local.
tips: Combine with Greenwich Park walk.

name: The Old Brewery Greenwich
description: A working microbrewery and pub in the Old Royal Naval College — Meantime Brewing's on-site microbrewery.
address: Pepys Building, Old Royal Naval College, London SE10 9LW
tips: Free brewery tours by appointment.

name: Coach & Horses Bruton Street
description: Mayfair Bruton Street pub dating to 1744 — wood-panelled, atmospheric, a rare gem on Mayfair's art-dealer street.
tips: Gets busy at 5pm with City-to-Mayfair crowd.

name: Scarfes Bar at Rosewood London
description: The cocktail bar at the Rosewood London — Gerald Scarfe-illustrated walls, live jazz, whisky tastings.
tips: Live jazz Fri/Sat.

name: Lyle Bar at Lyle's
description: Upstairs bar of Michelin-starred Lyle's — natural wines, fermented kombuchas, creative non-alcoholic cocktails.
address: Tea Building, 56 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6JJ
tips: Walk-in-friendly bar.

name: Bar Brosé
description: Covent Garden basement wine-bar — £22 'rosé all day' menu, natural-wine forward list.
tips: Bottomless rosé £35 weekends.

name: Discount Suit Company
description: Liverpool Street basement — originally a suit-warehouse turned speakeasy, with curious décor and serious cocktails.
tips: Walk-in if space; discreet 'DSC' sign.

name: Lab E20
description: Westfield Stratford City cocktail bar — rotating residencies, buzzing after-shopping destination.
tips: Happy hour 5-7pm.

name: The Lucky Pig
description: A tiny Piccadilly speakeasy — just 30 seats, and a whisky-forward menu. Discreet entrance.
tips: Follow the sign for 'Oxford Circus Underground' — the bar is behind.

name: The Marksman
description: Hackney Road gastropub — 19th-century exterior, Michelin Bib Gourmand-approved cooking, pub at its finest.
tips: Book for restaurant. Walk-in for bar.

name: The Duke of Sussex
description: Chiswick gastropub with a year-round garden — Spanish-leaning menu, seasonal tapas, a sharp wine list.
tips: Garden in summer.

name: Draft House
description: A beer-pub chain focused on craft beer — rotating casks, tasting flights, American-style food.
tips: Multiple branches. Good for introducing craft to the beer-curious.

name: The Bridge House
description: A London-Bridge-adjacent pub — 17th-century building, unreformed since the Georgians, a cornerstone.
tips: Sunday roast is a South-London classic.

name: The Crown & Anchor Brixton
description: Brixton's craft-beer community pub — 20+ taps, regular events, a strong local following.
tips: Quiz nights Tuesdays.

name: The Bell Aldgate
description: An Aldgate pub above the East End's oldest crossroads — history meets budget pints, near the former city gate.
tips: Close to Brick Lane.

name: Butler's Wharf Chop House
description: A riverside D&D pub-restaurant with Tower Bridge views — British menu, pub downstairs, terrace dining upstairs.
tips: Terrace for Tower Bridge sunset.

name: The Anchor & Hope Kingsland
description: Waterloo gastropub (distinct from The Anchor Bankside) — no-reservations, daily-changing menu, a cornerstone of the London dining scene.
tips: Queue for dinner; Sunday lunch seating 2pm bookable.

name: Fox & Anchor
description: A Smithfield pub open from 7am for 'market breakfasts' — traditional pub, serious breakfasts with ale on the side.
tips: 'City Boy' breakfast: bacon, eggs, black pudding, half pint of Guinness.

name: The Lockhouse
description: A converted East End lock-keeper's cottage turned pub — tiny, photogenic, riverside.
tips: Check exact location online — area developing.

name: The Dog & Wardrobe
description: A Dalston pub — unreformed, community-first, great cask ale selection.
tips: Local feel, quiz Tuesdays.

name: The Prince of Wales Putney
description: Putney's riverside Fuller's pub — Boat-Race viewing point, large terrace, pie-and-pint menu.
tips: Boat Race day (late March/early April) a London ritual.

name: The Elms
description: A Dulwich pub — wood-floored, dog-friendly, real fire in winter.
tips: Sunday roast.

name: Peckham Palms
description: A roof-terrace bar at the Aylesham Centre — summer-only, Caribbean-spirit cocktails, a Peckham weekend hit.
tips: Summer only. Tickets for some events.

name: Native at Browns
description: Browns Hotel's tiny natural-wine and seasonal-food bar — low-ceilinged, candle-lit, honest cooking.
tips: Book ahead — tiny.

name: Happiness Forgets Worship Street
description: The Worship Street sibling to Happiness Forgets — similar minimalism, different crowd.
tips: Walk-in-friendly first hour.
